messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 03:22 UTC - Cluster inf-prod-us-west-2: 4 nodes reported NotReady within 90s; affected k8s taint=pool=inference. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

sre_jordan: paging in. I see the alert, pulling metrics and events now. Which pools exactly? any customer 5xxs showing up?

runtime_emma: I can see spikes in 5xxs for /v1/generate from the hosted inference pool. Grafana shows increased container restarts coincident with node NotReady.

infra_li: kubelet heartbeat loss on nodes: inf-node-gpu-12, -15, -19. `systemd` shows kubelet restarting repeatedly. dmesg lines show repeated `NVRM: Xid` GPU errors on those hosts.

eng_oncall: @runtime_emma can you triage whether this is serving runtime OOMs vs node-level kernel issues? We should assess customer impact and start mitigation.

runtime_emma: quick findings: 1) Pod restarts show `OOMKilled` for launcher containers then failing to reattach GPU. 2) nvidia-driver logs show repeated ECC errors and then `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79` entries. 3) Some containers log `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` before process exit.

sre_jordan: likely a combination: hardware/driver errors causing kubelet flaps, causing pod churn and memory pressure across node. Immediate mitigation ideas: cordon and drain the affected nodes, scale up the inference ASG by +2, and trigger fallback route in routing policy to Dedicated for the most critical customers.

infra_li: I'm cordoning inf-node-gpu-12 and inf-node-gpu-15 now. Running: `kubectl cordon inf-node-gpu-12` then `kubectl drain inf-node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`.

infra_li: drain started; NOTE some pods are not terminating because they use local ephemeral cache. We'll force evict with `--grace-period=30 --timeout=5m`.

support_maya: Support note: we already have two customers (acme-inc, neurolytics) reporting increased latency/5xx. I'm opening a brief customer update and will add to status page if we see prolonged impact.

alice_product: Do we have a safe fallback model variant to route to? Product wants to avoid quality regressions but prefers uptime.

runtime_emma: For live traffic routing: we can shift critical customers to a quantized 8-bit variant with lower GPU mem footprint, same architecture. I'll prepare a canary rollout to the Dedicated pool for just the failing routes: `route: customer=acme-inc -> model=redwood-encoder-v2-8q`.

sre_jordan: Good. While infra finishes drains, I'll increase ASG desired count by 2 in us-west-2 and pre-warm nodes with `kubelet` + driver validation scripts. infra_li, can you coordinate image with latest driver hotfix?

infra_li: On it. Spinning up two pre-baked AMIs with driver 535.54. *ETA ~6min* to boot and join cluster. Will run healthcheck: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference -o wide` and check `nvidia-smi` on join.

eng_oncall: Reminder: take incident channel when ready. @sre_jordan -> @infra_li handed off ops lead.

sre_jordan: handing over to @infra_li for node replacement steps. I'm staying on for runbook and routing changes.

infra_li: New nodes joined: inf-node-gpu-24 and -25. nvidia-smi OK, no ECC errors. I'm uncordoning after validating kubelet stable: `kubectl uncordon inf-node-gpu-24`.

runtime_emma: I've kicked off routing override for acme-inc and neurolytics to Dedicated: `PATCH /routing/policies/overrides` with `targets: dedicated-usw2`. Verified requests are now landing in Dedicated and p99 latency dropped for those customers.

support_maya: posting update to customers: "We observed intermittent node-level GPU driver failures impacting inference in us-west-2. Traffic for affected customers has been routed to Dedicated capacity; we're replacing problematic hosts."

bob_customer_success: Received OK from acme-inc: their errors reduced to near zero after the switch. Neurolytics still seeing some retries but improving.

sre_jordan: monitoring cluster: kubelet restarts rate normalized after replacements. Node flaps count went from 4 -> 0 in last 12 minutes. Pod restart counts still stabilizing.

infra_li: Root cause hypothesis: a bad GPU driver/hardware combo triggered ECC/Xid errors leading to kernel-level GPU resets; kubelet timing out on tasks and flipping node Ready state. We'll open a ticket with cloud provider for hardware diagnostics and attach `dmesg`/`nvidia-smi -q` logs.

runtime_emma: Postmortem action items I'm adding now: 1) Add node-level GPU ECC/Xid alerting before kubelet NotReady. 2) Improve graceful evacuation for ephemeral cache pods (avoid local-data loss). 3) Add auto-fallback routing for customers with SLA tags to Dedicated when node flaps exceed threshold.

sre_jordan: On-call timeline note: incident started 03:22 UTC. Mitigations: cordon/drain + ASG scale up + route overrides performed by 03:38 UTC. Customer routing confirmed by 03:42 UTC. Declaration: mitigated at 03:45 UTC, monitoring for stability.

eng_oncall: Thanks all. @infra_li please file the cloud hardware ticket and attach logs. @runtime_emma please coordinate the follow-up rollout to ensure customers can be routed gracefully in future. I'll convert to a postmortem in /postmortems with RCA.

incident-bot: Incident update logged. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. SLA impact: partial for 18 minutes for some customers. Ticket ID INC-2026-3547
